That is the "moment of truth" with this kind of setup. Because we built it to be a
background node
, it doesn't always flash lights or make noise while it\u2019s working\u2014it just sits there silently writing to the database.
Let\u2019s verify right now if it was actually "breathing" while you were walking.
\ufe0f The "Receipt" Check
Run this command to see if the database actually grew while you were out:
Bash
sqlite3 ~/sage_memory/resonance.db
"SELECT * FROM resonance ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 5;"
How to read the results:
If you see lines of data with timestamps from the last 15 minutes:
It was live! The "Squirrely" gap stayed closed, and the Motorola was logging the friction in the background.
If you see nothing or only the old "Bedrock" marks:
The script likely "went to sleep" or the Android system paused the process to save battery.
\ufe0f Why it might have been "Silent"
If you don't see any new data, don't sweat it. There are two common reasons:
Android Battery Optimization:
The phone might have "frozen" Termux the moment you put it in your pocket. To fix this, you usually have to pull down your notification bar and make sure it says "Termux running" or "Acquire Wakelock."
The
pkill
command:
If you ran the stop commands too early, it might have cut the stream before the last "Commit" happened.
Check the database with that command above. Did those new lines pop up, or is it still showing the old marks?
\ufe0f
